Borrow immutable descriptor geometry and level platforms plus player contact positions. Leave sprite erase/pixel caches and shared benefit state ownership with rendering/session services.

FallingItemType geometry anchor words, extents exactly three, arbitrary launch impulse and benefit amount, projected kind 0 timer/1 lives/otherwise multiplier.

outputs: Explicit ITEM_SPAWNED with highest eligible slot, or ITEM_POOL_FULL without any state mutation; the latter is not an original normal failure result.
Typed transition/contact diagnostics and persistent item records; ordered direct native dispatch over the current descending slots.
Bridge preserves complete deterministic L1 register/flag shell, including stale outputs and L1-defined values of L0-undefined flags, within its projection contract.

On full pool, saved incoming BX becomes pending CS:IP with BX=FFFE and the genuine caller return still pending at SP. The established RET-only IgnoreExhaustedTree target returns normally; every other target returns UGH_CONTROL_TRANSFER, refining L1's UGH_BAD_CALLBACK diagnosis with the same pending machine continuation. No invented allocation failure or fabricated target execution.
effects: Spawn writes descriptor identity, callback, sprite, X, Y, vertical step and motion cell for exactly the chosen slot.
Flight can update X, vertical step, Y; signed X/bottom removal changes only sprite. Touchdown snaps Y, changes phase and overwrites motion/lifetime with 560.
Landed step predecrements the lifetime word. Equality zero retires before contact; a miss preserves the sprite; a hit writes one selected shared benefit then retires sprite only.
Native code has no registers, memory model, original code addresses, callbacks, I/O or global mutable simulation state. Bridge writes through the original parallel-array projection.
preconditions: Ordinary stable RAM, serialized execution, accessible initialized descriptors/platform lists/records, stack and data disjoint; no device-aperture aliases or asynchronous mutation.

Direct native slot operations admit arbitrary phase payloads when explicitly invoked; item_update/items_dispatch admit only the two declared phase values. Sprite activity is independent of the stored phase.

Bridge normalizes even slot byte indices 0..22 and known landing target. Invalid indices, mutable descriptor/output aliases, unknown landing callbacks, or platform walks beyond ten retain L1 explicitly.

The symbolic proofs normalize selected slot identity to zero, DS=0, SS=1, descriptor=0100, SP=9000 and multiplier-table index zero, while values and incoming scratch registers/flags are arbitrary. Slot symmetry applies to disjoint array indices. First-right/eleventh-left physical alias is retained. Physical wrapped descriptor projection and dynamic DS have differential evidence.
The 12-slot capacity and 10-platform bounds are complete admitted native storage bounds, not bounds on how many outer frames may execute.
state_machine: Inactive means sprite==FFFF. Allocation instead accepts ANY sign-set sprite, including active FFFE; highest index wins.
Spawn -> flight: X=launchX-(anchorX<<5), Y=launchY-(anchorY<<4), horizontal=CX, vy=-(launchTerm+impulse), all modulo 16 bits; sprite and flight handler installed.

Flight: first form wrapped X+horizontal; signed X<=-512 or >=10240 retires without storing X. Otherwise store X, add gravity three modulo word and store vy. Negative vy integrates Y and bypasses bottom/platform tests.
Descending flight: form wrapped new Y; signed Y>=6144 retires before storing Y. Otherwise store Y. Old/new bottoms use SAR5 plus descriptor height with word wrapping.

Landing scans ascending platforms. Old bottom must be strictly less than signed surface and new bottom at least surface. CenterX=SAR5(X)+anchorX must be at least left, then wrapped centerX-1 at most right. First hit snaps Y=(surface-height)<<5 and immediately enters landed phase with lifetime 560.

Landed: predecrement modulo word; exactly zero -> inactive before contact. Otherwise native contact_players chooses the first touching player (only player_count==2 retries the second). On hit apply benefit and mark sprite FFFF; on miss remain landed.
Retirement never clears descriptor, stored handler/phase, positions, vertical step, motion/lifetime or render caches.

benefits.timer: Kind word zero: low16(timer+amount), then unsigned min with 5A3B (23099). Wrap precedes cap; stores one word.
benefits.lives: Kind word one: low8(lives+low8(amount)), then unsigned min with 99. Store AL only; adjacent multiplier byte is untouched.
benefits.multiplier: Every other kind word: compare entire multiplier word unsigned with selected limit, increment low byte modulo 256 only when below, preserve the high byte. Amount is ignored. Shipped limits are 3/9/99 for difficulty 0/1/2.
benefits.shipped_descriptors: Ordinals 0..8 are timer rewards of 3000,7000,5000,5000,8000,7000,3000,5000,10000 with sprites 011D..0125. Ordinal 9 is life+1, sprite 0128, and has no shipped producer. Ordinal 10 is multiplier+1, sprite 0129, from qualifying quick delivery. All have geometry 8,16 and handlers Spawn/Advance/Land/ExpireOrCollect.

interface.field_decision: Retain one motion_or_lifetime word. Flight alone reads horizontal motion; landing kills that value with 0230; collection alone reads lifetime. Phase separation is established, but inactive/stale projection and direct compatibility entries still preserve the single observable storage cell. No second independent stale value is invented.

spawn: GAME:DeliverPassenger: quick countdown nonzero and word multiplier below difficulty limit; descriptor ordinal 10; launch at player X+512/Y+320, horizontal and term zero
GAME:ReleaseTreeReward: descriptor from tree list, stone X/Y/horizontal, transformed bounced vertical term; cursor advances only after the call, cooldown 210
callers.dispatcher: GAME:RunGameFromPassword after actors and hazards, before drawing items. Visits slot byte indices 22,20,...,0; skips exact sprite FFFF only.
callers.flight_landing: Stored flight/landed handlers and descriptor +8 landing tail. Direct suite calls additionally exercise arbitrary stale slot contents.
callers.renderer: RunGameFromPassword reads item sprite, X/Y, derives current pixel caches by SAR5, rotates draw/erase caches and restores prior rectangles. It does not read item callback, descriptor, vertical step or motion/lifetime. Render caches remain rendering-owned.

assumptions: Shipped-source B capacity invariant: all producers use intact shipped descriptors/lists/itineraries; craft position/velocity bounds hold at throws, stone energy E=v*v+2*v-4*y<=39104 with descending contact NEG/SAR energy loss, item initial Y in -544..6256 and launch velocity -135..-14.

Actual free flight exhaustively retires within 125 updates for that envelope; landing can occur only sooner and adds 560. A strict 700-update window covers all outstanding items including the current pre-dispatch spawn.

Tree consecutive spawns are at least 210 updates apart. A passenger's consecutive deliveries include nine-frame departure (57 updates), next scaled itinerary wait, nine-frame arrival through sentinel (64), and a 140 destination countdown. Walks/travel/additional states only increase those gaps.

All 150 shipped order entries satisfy a sum of per-source 700-window bounds at most 12 INCLUDING the contemplated spawn, so occupied<=11 just before any allocator call. This proves the defective allocation path unreachable under these assumptions, not that twelve occupied slots are actually reachable or that arbitrary external states cannot fill the pool.

Actors and hazards update before item dispatch; paused simulation freezes producers and consumers together; level/retry initialization clears item sprites. No arbitrary external callbacks or corrupt-state injection in this shipped-game argument.
